news.headline: Exchanged RSUs Settle: NeurAxis Issues About 592,000 Shares to CEO, CMO and Chief Regulatory Officer
news.summary: Form 4s filed August 26 show shares delivered on August 24 under the option-for-RSU exchange: 199,188 to CEO Brian Carrico, 199,106 to CMO Adrian Miranda and 193,678 to Chief Regulatory Officer Thomas Carrico, roughly 592,000 shares in total. The same filings show 320,000 legacy options converted for Brian Carrico and 337,204 for Miranda, turning underwater paper into real share count against a base of roughly 12.5 million shares outstanding.

news.headline: NeurAxis 8-K Details Completed Option Exchange Plus New Three-Year Management and Director Equity Grants
news.summary: The option-for-RSU exchange approved by shareholders on June 10 went effective July 24, cancelling 1,319,394 options and issuing an equal number of immediately vesting RSUs. On August 13 the compensation committee added three-year-vesting grants priced at $6.28 - 193,329 RSUs to Brian Carrico, 141,479 to CFO Timothy Henrichs, 133,341 to Adrian Miranda and 135,906 to Thomas Carrico - plus one-time share awards to independent directors Kristin Ferge (31,134), Bradley Watkins (26,073) and Jane Keyser (26,073) after a consultant found pay below market.

news.headline: NRXS Stock Dips Post Q2 Earnings Despite Revenue Surge and Gross Margin Gain
news.summary: Shares fell 8.6% in the days after the August 11 print versus a 0.3% gain for the S&P 500, as the wider-than-expected loss outweighed the revenue beat. The review highlighted IB-Stim unit deliveries up 60% year over year, gross margin at 85.9%, traction with two large commercial payers and the first commercial activity in the Veterans Affairs channel.

news.headline: NeurAxis Reports Record Q2 2026 Results: Revenue Up 116%, but EPS Miss and Going-Concern Language Persist
news.summary: Q2 revenue rose 115.7% year over year to $1.93M on 60% unit growth, gross margin expanded 230 basis points to 85.9%, and average selling price rose 28% to $992 as the Category I CPT code 64567 pushed more devices to full reimbursement. On the call management said 24 commercial insurers now have formal PENFS policies covering over 100 million lives and prior-authorization approvals improved to 31% from 12%, but EPS of -$0.19 missed the -$0.16 consensus, opex jumped 53% to $3.8M, and the going-concern qualification stayed in place despite $8.3M of cash at June 30.

news.headline: Resale Prospectus for 1.92 Million Insider and Employee Shares Goes Effective, Adding Potential Supply
news.summary: The S-3 filed July 23 was declared effective August 3 and the final prospectus followed on August 6, registering 1,923,194 shares for resale by selling stockholders - 849,212 already-issued shares, 923,776 underlying RSUs and 150,206 director service shares. That is about 15% of the 12,477,309 shares outstanding as of July 22 and includes stakes held by CEO Brian Carrico (213,445 registered), CFO Timothy Henrichs (231,591) and former director Christopher Brown (792,837).

news.headline: NeurAxis Expands Payer Coverage with New Policies, Adding Over 500,000 Covered Lives
news.summary: New medical policies for PENFS added more than 500,000 covered lives, expanding access to IB-Stim for beneficiaries in the Mid-Atlantic region. CEO Brian Carrico framed the regional wins as building momentum toward comprehensive nationwide written policy coverage while talks with the nation's largest payers continue.

catalysts.label: VA sales force fully staffed
catalysts.detail: Management committed on the August 11 call to having 10 commission-only (1099) Veterans Affairs territory representatives in the field by September 15, 2026 - now about a week away. The VA Federal Supply Schedule contract for IB-Stim has been live since December 1, 2025, opening a system that serves nearly 7 million patients a year, and management says early VA adoption is running ahead of expectations. This hire is the step that should turn opportunistic VA orders into a measurable Q4 volume line, and the Q3 call in November is the first place investors will see whether the 10 reps were actually seated on time.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings
catalysts.detail: Next quarterly report, expected in the first half of November on the company's usual cadence (Q1 on May 12, Q2 on August 11). Key tests: whether triple-digit revenue growth holds against a tougher comparison, whether ASP keeps climbing from $992 toward the $1,195 list price, whether the going-concern qualification can finally be dropped, and how much of the promised H2 step-up in sales, marketing, clinical and policy hiring eats into cash burn on an $8.3M June-30 balance. First quarter with a fully staffed VA channel and the Mid-Atlantic policies live.

catalysts.label: Major national payer coverage decision
catalysts.detail: Talks with two large commercial payers gained traction in Q2 and management is cautiously optimistic about a coverage win in H2 2026 or early 2027. The CEO has framed a single large national payer add as the step that could slingshot the company toward profitability, since hospitals generally want roughly 70% of their patient population covered before adopting broadly. Twenty-four commercial insurers currently have formal PENFS policies covering over 100 million lives; a top-five national payer would be a step change rather than the usual 0.5-1.25 million-life regional additions.

catalysts.label: RED commercial ramp and additional PENFS indications
catalysts.detail: The Rectal Expulsion Device received FDA 510(k) clearance in December 2024 as a screening tool for chronic constipation and pelvic floor dysfunction in adults, and already carries a Category I CPT code with Medicare and broad commercial coverage - so it needs distribution, not reimbursement work. Separately, PENFS is in randomized trials for post-concussion syndrome, cyclic vomiting syndrome, opioid-sparing post-operative pain and fibromyalgia, any of which could support a future 510(k) label expansion beyond the pediatric FAP/functional dyspepsia franchise.

catalysts.label: State Medicaid adoption of CPT 64567
catalysts.detail: Many states still have not added CPT code 64567 to their fee schedules, leaving no payment methodology and blocking coverage for Medicaid beneficiaries even though the Category I code has been in effect since January 1, 2026. Each state that loads the code onto its schedule unlocks a new reimbursed patient pool, and Medicaid is disproportionately important in pediatric gastroenterology. The 2027 fee-schedule update cycle is the next broad opportunity for states to add it.

catalysts.label: Covered lives above 200 million
catalysts.detail: Management reiterated on the Q2 call that it expects to exceed 200 million covered lives by the end of 2027, roughly doubling from the 100 million-plus reached today, with the CEO saying he would be highly disappointed to miss that level. Reaching it would effectively cover the full serviceable market and requires a steady run of payer-policy wins like the August Mid-Atlantic addition, ideally anchored by at least one national payer.

pulse: NRXS is sitting around $5.96-$6.10 for a market cap near $75M on about 12.6 million shares, against $8.3M of cash at June 30 and a bullish but thin analyst set (2 Buy ratings, median target $11, Craig-Hallum $13, low $9). The August 11 Q2 print validated the CPT-code reimbursement thesis - revenue up 116% to $1.93M, gross margin 85.9%, ASP up 28% to $992, prior-authorization approvals at 31% versus 12% a year ago - but the stock fell about 9% because EPS of -$0.19 missed, opex jumped 53%, and the going-concern qualification stayed. Nothing has been announced since August 26 and there are no SEC filings or press releases in September at all, so the stock is drifting in a genuine news vacuum with three operational items to watch: the 10-rep VA sales force due September 15, the two large commercial payers in negotiation, and state Medicaid programs loading CPT 64567 onto their fee schedules.
